title: Which runtime does M2 build the state machine on?
lead: Re-scored with the state machine inside VOS, at vos-core 5c78975 on Linux with the JIT, both candidates pass all 17 host-contract rows (VOS's three after-computed rows on its faults build, which can hold commits). On three nodes VOS passed every replication, damage and upgrade row it could run (R-04b's run recorded no evidence that its damage took effect); the purpose-built store has no replication, lost acknowledged records on a restore, and lost one on a damaged last frame, where VOS's single-node damage left no trace, probably because it never reached an acknowledged append.
bullets: VOS on three nodes lost no acknowledged record across 21 leader kills, each with a submit in flight as last seen, a replica replaced, and a replica's disk lost.
The purpose-built store is faster on one disk, about 4,500 to 4,800 records/s against VOS's 239 to 2,979, but has only restore to recover with.
A 100k-record halted swap takes about 59 to 82 s on VOS and 3.0 s on the store: VOS's total-loss recovery time.

Before v0: pin and mirror VOS's forks, port contracts/ to no_std under DEC-4, accept or fix G-54 (its single-node residual, and damage to a leader's append, are untested), and check the JIT on the production host.
rec: VOS as the whole runtime, because only it survives losing a node or a disk without losing acknowledged records.
options: VOS as the whole runtime for M2, three replicas, at a pinned and mirrored commit (recommended)
Purpose-built store for M2; drop VOS for v0
